title: The Bhagavad Gita
description: Based on HH Sri Raghavendra Teertha's Gita Vivruti

verses.translation: Dhrutarashtra said: O Sanjaya! Assembled at Kuru Kshetra, the designated land for committing righteous acts (Field of Righteousness), what did my clan of Kauravas and Pandavas do?
Sanjaya said: King Duryodhana, upon seeing the formation of the Pandavas' army, immediately rushed to his teacher Drona, and said as follows.
O My Teacher! Look at the formation of the mighty army of Pandavas which has been organized by your clever student Dhrushtadyumna, son of Drupada.
Possessing heavy weapons are the brave warriors Yuyudhana (Satyaki), Virata, and King Drupada, all Maharathas. They are as capable as Bheema and Arjuna.
Other brave warriors include Drushtaketu, Chekitana, Kashiraja who are extraordinarily strong, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shybhya who are superior among men.
Yudhamanyu, the brave warrior, Uttamowja, the strong warrior, Abhimanyu, son of Subhadra, and sons of Draupadi are also here. They too are Maharathas.
O Drona! Superior among the wise men! Now I will enumerate the great warriors from our side. So, please listen with attention.
Our side includes yourself, Bheeshma, Karna, Krupa who has won many wars, Ashwatthama, Vikarna and Bhoorishravas, son of Somadatta.
Along with them are many warriors ready to sacrifice their lives for my sake. They are all well versed in wars and are armed with heavy weapons.
But our army headed by Bheeshma is not strong enough to defeat them. While their army headed by Bheema can defeat us.
Hence all of you need to position yourselves in your designated spots in the formations and guard Bheeshma, our commander.
To cheer up Duryodhana, the valiant grandfather Bheeshma, the eldest of the Kurus, blew his conch shell loudly, producing a sound like the roar of a lion.
